drafted_from: tool:choose-which-ai-answers-me's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make the request that sets which AI answers a person, or sends them back to automatic routing, as the selected-agent part sends it to the workflow slot, without sending it", with {"agent_id":"agent:sample-writer"}. It runs tool:choose-which-ai-answers-me and answers {"request":{"target":"slot::workflow","payload":{"operation":"execute_definition","include_output":false,"definition_id":"action:update-selected-agent","input":{"value":"agent:sample-writer"}}},"automatic":false}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Make the request that sets which AI answers a person, or sends them back to automatic routing, as the selected-agent part sends it to the workflow slot, without sending it", and give it agent_id (The AI that should answer, or "" for automatic routing.).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:choose-which-ai-answers-me and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Give agent_id: the AI that should answer the person, or "" to go back to automatic routing (and, rarely, definition_id: the workflow definition that keeps the choice, action:update-selected-agent when left out).
